questions.question: What is the natural real domain of the function f(x) = √(\fracx - 2)x + 5 ?
questions.explanation: We require (x - 2/x + 5) ≥ 0 and x + 5 ≠ 0 . Using a sign diagram with critical points at x = -5 and x = 2 : when x > 2 , (+)/(+) > 0 ; when -5 < x < 2 , (-)/(+) < 0 ; when x < -5 , (-)/(-) > 0 . Hence, domain is (-∞, -5) \cup [2, ∞) .

questions.question: Why does the function f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 7 defined on ℝ not possess an inverse function f^-1(x) ?
options: It is not one-to-one (fails the horizontal line test across ℝ )
It is not continuous across the real line
The range is strictly limited to non-negative integers
Its derivative is identically zero everywhere
questions.explanation: A function has an inverse if and only if it is bijective (both one-to-one and onto). A parabola opens upwards with vertex at x = 2 , so horizontal lines for y > 3 intersect the curve twice, violating the one-to-one requirement.

questions.question: Where does the curve f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 2 have a point of inflexion?
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 9 . f''(x) = 6x - 12 . Setting f''(x) = 0 ⇒ 6x = 12 ⇒ x = 2 . Since f''(x) changes sign at x = 2 (negative for x < 2 , positive for x > 2 ), x = 2 is a point of inflexion. Value f(2) = 2^3 - 6(2^2) + 9(2) + 2 = 8 - 24 + 18 + 2 = 4 . Point is (2, 4) .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 5.8: Points of Inflexion

questions.question: A particle moves with velocity v(t) = 2t - 4 m/s . What is the total distance traveled by the particle between t = 0 and t = 3 ?
questions.explanation: Velocity changes sign at 2t - 4 = 0 ⇒ t = 2 . Total distance = ∫_0^3 |v(t)| dt = ∫_0^2 -(2t - 4) dt + ∫_2^3 (2t - 4) dt . First segment: [-t^2 + 4t]_0^2 = -4 + 8 = 4 m . Second segment: [t^2 - 4t]_2^3 = (9 - 12) - (4 - 8) = -3 - (-4) = 1 m . Total distance = 4 + 1 = 5 m . (Displacement is -3 m ).
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 5.9: Kinematics (Total Distance)

questions.question: Using integration by parts, what is ∫ x cos x dx ?
options: x sin x + cos x + C
x sin x - cos x + C
x cos x - sin x + C
